meta.label: Banking
meta.attribution: Where your money sleeps is one of the biggest votes it casts. This covers everyday and current accounts at banks serving the US, UK and EU, plus the credit union route generally. Fossil-fuel financing figures are read directly off the league table in the Banking on Climate Chaos 2026 report (data year 2025), published by Rainforest Action Network, BankTrack, the Center for Energy, Ecology and Development, Indigenous Environmental Network, Oil Change International, Reclaim Finance, Sierra Club and Urgewald; it tracks the world's 65 largest fossil financiers, so a bank too small to appear on it carries no score on this axis rather than an assumed good one. Three mission banks here are checked instead against the Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty's own list of endorsing banks. Ownership and legal form come from each bank's own statutory register: UK Companies House for UK-incorporated banks, the FCA's Mutuals Public Register for building societies, and the US Securities and Exchange Commission's EDGAR system for US public companies. Certification is checked against B Lab's own Certified B Corporation directory and the Global Alliance for Banking on Values' own site, not a brand's own badge. Complaint counts cover checking and savings account complaints in the CFPB Consumer Complaint Database, searched directly by company name for complaints received January 2024 through December 2025, for the US-chartered banks the database covers; these are raw counts, not adjusted for how many accounts a bank has open, so a large national bank will show more complaints than a small one even if its rate of trouble is no worse. Not every cell is filled for every bank: where a register does not cover an option, or a fact could not be checked against a primary source, the cell is left empty rather than guessed. Not financial advice. Reviewed 2026-08. Dispute or correct any rating via Contribute.

products.name: Triodos Bank
products.description: A European sustainability bank that lends only to social, cultural and environmental projects, and publishes every organisation it finances.

environment.note: The Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty's own list of the 25 GABV banks that endorsed the Treaty in 2024 describes Triodos as the first bank in the world to sign up to the Treaty initiative, and among the leading lenders for clean energy projects.

ethics.note: B Lab's own directory lists Triodos Bank N.V. as a Certified B Corporation since March 2015, with an overall B Impact score of 131.3 against a median of 50.9 for ordinary businesses that complete the assessment.

transparency.note: Triodos states: "We believe that sustainable banking depends on trust and transparency, so we publish details of the organisations we lend to."

fees.note: Triodos Bank's own fee information document lists a flat £3 monthly fee for maintaining its UK personal current account, with no listed way to waive it.

accessibility.note: B Lab's certification profile lists Triodos Bank N.V. as operating in Belgium, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Spain and the United Kingdom.

products.name: GLS Bank
products.description: Germany's pioneering social-ecological bank, a member-owned cooperative that finances renewable energy, organic farming and social projects.

environment.note: GLS Bank appears in the Global Alliance for Banking on Values' own member case studies, but the Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty's list of the 25 GABV banks that formally endorsed the Treaty in 2024 does not name GLS Bank, searched August 2026, so this comparison does not carry the same Treaty-endorsement fact for it that it does for Triodos, Beneficial State and Amalgamated.

ethics.note: GLS Bank's own legal notice states it is registered as GLS Gemeinschaftsbank eG, an eingetragene Genossenschaft (registered cooperative), in the cooperative register of the Amtsgericht Bochum under number 224, and supervised by Germany's Federal Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin).

fees.note: GLS Bank's own page on the GLS Beitrag states customers pay an annual contribution of 60 euros (5 euros a month) from age 28, or 12 euros a year (1 euro a month) under 28 or with income at or below the tax-free threshold, collected as one sum each January; this is separate from any account-specific fee.

products.name: Beneficial State Bank
products.description: A West-Coast community bank majority-owned by a nonprofit foundation, so its economic rights are held in the public interest rather than by private shareholders.

environment.note: The Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty's own list of the 25 GABV banks that endorsed the Treaty in 2024 names Beneficial State Bank among them.

ethics.note: B Lab's own directory lists Beneficial State Bank as a Certified B Corporation since September 2012, with an overall B Impact score of 153.6, and describes it as a mission-driven bank under a unique nonprofit ownership model.

fees.note: Beneficial State Bank's own checking page lists a Checking account with a $5 monthly service charge, waived with a $500 average balance, $10,000 combined average balance, or $500 in monthly direct deposits, alongside a separate eChecking account with a $0 monthly charge if statements are electronic.

accessibility.note: Beneficial State Bank's own checking page states it has branches in California, Oregon and Washington, plus a network of thousands of surcharge-free ATMs coast to coast in the United States.

complaints.note: The CFPB Consumer Complaint Database returns zero complaints under the company name Beneficial State Bank, searched for all products and all dates in August 2026. A bank this small can have no complaints on file simply because too few customers have filed one by that exact name, so this absence is not the same finding as a large bank's low count.

products.name: Climate First Bank
products.description: A Florida-based, fully digital community bank built around climate, with a major solar-lending book, though it is not itself listed as a GABV member or a Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty endorser.

environment.note: Climate First Bank's own impact page states it has financed over $427 million in residential solar, with 30.8 percent of that directed to low-to-moderate income communities, and that in 2025 alone it lent over $500 million into what it calls values-driven projects, including rooftop solar, affordable housing and small businesses. The page does not itself state a policy of declining to lend to fossil-fuel companies.

ethics.note: B Lab's own directory lists Climate First Bancorp as a Certified B Corporation since July 2023, with an overall B Impact score of 98.6.

fees.note: Reporting on Climate First Bank's checking accounts states all of its checking products carry no monthly service fee and no minimum balance requirement, with a $5 monthly charge only for customers who choose paper statements over electronic ones.

complaints.note: The CFPB Consumer Complaint Database returns zero complaints under the company names Climate First Bank and Climate First Bancorp, Inc., searched for all products and all dates in August 2026. A bank this small can have no complaints on file simply because too few customers have filed one by that exact name.

products.name: Amalgamated Bank
products.description: A century-old, labour-rooted US bank and a Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty endorser, though it is a publicly traded company on Nasdaq rather than a cooperative or foundation-owned bank.

environment.note: The Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty's own list of the 25 GABV banks that endorsed the Treaty in 2024 names Amalgamated Bank first among them. Separately, Amalgamated's own announcement of its 100% Fossil Fuel Free Portfolio describes an investment product for customers, screened to exclude coal, oil and gas, and fossil-fired utility companies; that describes an investment option the bank offers rather than a claim about its entire loan book.

ethics.note: B Lab's own directory lists Amalgamated Bank as a Certified B Corporation since January 2017. Its most recent Form 10-K, filed with the SEC, shows it trades publicly on Nasdaq under ticker AMAL, so it answers to public shareholders rather than a cooperative or foundation structure.

transparency.note: Amalgamated Financial Corp. files an annual Form 10-K with the SEC, the disclosure required of every US public reporting company.

fees.note: Amalgamated Bank's own page states its Everyday Impact Checking account carries a $0 monthly maintenance fee with no conditions, while its Maximum Impact Checking account carries a $0 fee with a qualifying direct deposit or $10 a month without one.

complaints.note: The CFPB Consumer Complaint Database returns zero complaints under the company name Amalgamated Bank, searched for all products and all dates in August 2026. A bank this small can have no complaints on file simply because too few customers have filed one by that exact name.

products.name: Tomorrow
products.description: A German mobile-first banking provider whose deposits are channelled into climate and impact projects. It has no banking licence of its own and operates on partner bank Solaris SE's German licence.

environment.note: Tomorrow's own sustainability page states customer money is screened against more than 100 positive and negative criteria by an independent Impact Council, is invested in renewable energy, sustainable infrastructure and affordable housing, and avoids the industries it says conventional banks fund, including fossil fuels, factory farming and tobacco.

ethics.note: Tomorrow holds no banking licence itself; its accounts are provided by partner Solaris SE, which holds a full German banking licence (a CRR credit institution licence) issued by BaFin in 2017 and is also supervised by the European Central Bank.

accessibility.note: Solaris SE's own licence page states that as an EU-licensed bank it can passport its services across other EU and EEA member states, which is the basis for Tomorrow's reach beyond Germany.

products.name: The Co-operative Bank
products.description: A UK bank with a customer-led Ethical Policy since 1992, and since January 2025 back inside the mutual sector as a subsidiary of Coventry Building Society.

environment.note: The Co-operative Bank's own values and ethics page states its customer-led Ethical Policy excludes fossil-fuel extraction, and gives the example that it has previously declined to open an account for an organisation because of its involvement in fossil-fuel extraction.

ethics.note: The Co-operative Bank's own press release states that Coventry Building Society completed its acquisition of The Co-operative Bank on 2 January 2025, making the Bank a subsidiary of Coventry Building Society and bringing it back under mutual ownership after being shareholder and hedge-fund owned.

transparency.note: Companies House lists The Co-operative Bank P.L.C. (company number 00990937) as an active public limited company that files annual accounts, currently with The Co-operative Bank Finance P.L.C. registered as its person with significant control.

products.name: Nationwide Building Society
products.description: The world's largest building society, owned by its members, with no shareholders and no stock-market listing.

environment.note: Nationwide's own responsible investment page states its treasury holdings are restricted to government bonds, covered bonds and consumer-finance-backed securities, and that as a result it does not lend directly to high-emitting sectors such as the fossil-fuel industry. This describes the shape of its investment portfolio rather than an active screening policy of the kind Triodos or Beneficial State publish.

ethics.note: The FCA's Mutuals Public Register lists Nationwide Building Society as Registered under registration number 355B, a Building Society under the Building Societies Act 1986, originally registered on 22 June 1875, which as a legal form has no shareholders.

fees.note: Nationwide's own FlexAccount page states: "Our everyday bank account that lets you bank your way. No monthly fee."

accessibility.note: Nationwide's own FlexAccount page says it keeps 'Over 600 branches across the UK', that the account can be moved in with the Current Account Switch Service, and that its app is 'Rated 4.8 stars in App Store and 4.8 stars in Google Play'.

products.name: Local credit union
products.description: A US not-for-profit financial cooperative owned and controlled by its members. Member ownership is meaningful governance evidence, but not proof of a fossil-free loan book, and complaint and fee data cannot be scored for a generic category.

environment.note: NCUA says one member's savings becomes another member's loan. That does not establish a fossil-free loan book; check the individual credit union's current lending and investment policies.

ethics.note: NCUA describes US credit unions as not-for-profit institutions owned and controlled by their members, with surplus returned through member benefits rather than external shareholders.

transparency.note: Members elect the board, but public lending and climate disclosure still varies by individual credit union.

products.name: Monzo
products.description: A popular UK app-only bank, privately owned through a holding company backed by venture-capital investors rather than by its customers.

environment.note: Monzo's own business practices page states it only invests customer deposits in safe, high-quality government and quasi-government bonds, that most deposits are held at central banks, and that it does not invest in fossil-fuel based energy companies, arms companies or tobacco companies.

ethics.note: Companies House lists Monzo Bank Holding Group Limited as the person with significant control of Monzo Bank Limited, notified 12 September 2023, owning 75 percent or more of shares and voting rights; the prior PSC was a venture-capital fund, Passion Capital FS (GP) LLP. Monzo is a privately held, shareholder-owned company, not a cooperative or mutual.

fees.note: Monzo's own current account page states: "Our current accounts are free and we don't charge monthly fees or surprise you with hidden costs." Paid Monzo Plans start at £3 a month for extra features.

accessibility.note: Monzo's own current account page says '16 million customers bank with Monzo' and rates its app 4.9 on the App Store and 4.8 on Google Play, with switching by the Current Account Switch Service. The same page says that if you 'don't currently meet the criteria to open an account with Monzo' it points you to Citizens Advice or MoneyHelper, so the account is not open to everyone.

products.name: Starling Bank
products.description: A UK app bank with a published ethics statement excluding fossil-fuel investment, though, like Monzo, it is a privately held company backed by outside investors rather than customer-owned.

environment.note: Starling's own ethics statement states plainly: "We do not invest in the fossil fuel industry."

ethics.note: Companies House lists Starling Intermediate Holdings Limited as the person with significant control of Starling Bank Limited, notified 30 September 2025, owning 75 percent or more of shares and voting rights; the prior PSC was Starling Group Holdings Limited. Starling is a privately held, shareholder-owned company, not a cooperative or mutual.

products.name: bunq
products.description: A pan-European app bank licensed and supervised by the Dutch central bank, with an opt-in socially responsible investing option that screens out fossil fuels.

environment.note: bunq's own site describes "socially responsible investing" as a feature that lets customers invest in companies selected with social and environmental criteria in mind, while avoiding sectors like fossil fuels, weapons and tobacco; the page frames this as an investing option rather than a blanket policy covering every customer's deposits.

ethics.note: bunq's own legal imprint states bunq B.V. is registered with the Dutch Chamber of Commerce (Kamer van Koophandel), registration number 54992060, and is supervised by De Nederlandsche Bank, with branch registrations listed in Germany, France, Spain, Ireland, Italy and Belgium.

accessibility.note: bunq's own legal imprint lists registered branches or representatives in the Netherlands, Germany, France, Spain, Ireland, Italy and Belgium.

products.name: Chime
products.description: A fee-light US banking app that holds no bank charter of its own; deposits sit at partner banks The Bancorp Bank and Stride Bank. It went public on Nasdaq in 2025 and publishes no fossil-free lending policy, because it does not itself make loans funded by customer deposits the way a chartered bank does.

ethics.note: Chime's own help centre states Chime is a financial technology company, not a bank, and that banking services are provided by The Bancorp Bank, N.A. or Stride Bank, N.A., both FDIC members. Chime Financial, Inc.'s Form 10-K, filed with the SEC, shows it trades publicly on Nasdaq under ticker CHYM.

fees.note: Chime's own site states its checking account has no monthly fees and no minimum balance fees.

fees.note: Capital One's own page states: "There are no monthly fees with a Capital One 360 Checking account," and "no fees to open, keep or use" it.

products.name: Ally Bank
products.description: A branchless US bank, mostly auto finance and deposits. It is not among the 65 banks the Banking on Climate Chaos report tracks, so this comparison carries no fossil-financing figure for it either way.

ethics.note: Ally Financial Inc.'s most recent Form 10-K, filed with the SEC, confirms it is a publicly traded company (NYSE: ALLY) that answers to public shareholders.

products.name: Lloyds Banking Group
products.description: A big UK high-street bank, and the smallest fossil financier of the five UK majors on the 2026 Banking on Climate Chaos league table, though still a conventional shareholder-owned bank.

environment.note: The Banking on Climate Chaos 2026 league table ranks Lloyds Banking Group 54th of the 65 banks it tracks, with $1.7 billion in fossil-fuel financing in 2025, the lowest figure of the five UK banks the report names.

ethics.note: Companies House states the PSC information for Lloyds Banking Group PLC is not available because, from 26 November 2018, the company has been exempt from the requirement to obtain PSC information as it has voting shares admitted to trading on a UK regulated market; it is registered as a public limited company.

products.name: NatWest Group
products.description: A major UK high-street bank, the second-smallest fossil financier of the five UK majors on the 2026 Banking on Climate Chaos league table, though still a conventional shareholder-owned bank.

environment.note: The Banking on Climate Chaos 2026 league table ranks NatWest Group 49th of the 65 banks it tracks, with $2.5 billion in fossil-fuel financing in 2025.

ethics.note: Companies House states the PSC information for NatWest Group PLC is not available because, from 25 January 2018, the company has been exempt from the requirement to obtain PSC information as it has voting shares admitted to trading on a UK regulated market; it is registered as a public limited company.

fees.note: NatWest's own page for the Select account states: "Fee-free current account. There's no monthly account fee for this standard bank account."

accessibility.note: NatWest's own Select Account page offers the Current Account Switch Service and face-to-face help either 'over video (criteria applies) or in branch'. Its app is 'available to Online Banking customers with compatible iOS and Android devices and a UK or international mobile number in specific countries'.

products.name: Santander UK
products.description: The UK arm of Banco Santander. The fossil-financing figure below is for the Santander group worldwide, since Banking on Climate Chaos does not report a UK-only figure.

environment.note: The Banking on Climate Chaos 2026 league table ranks Santander (the group, not the UK subsidiary alone) 21st of the 65 banks it tracks, with $16.8 billion in fossil-fuel financing in 2025.

ethics.note: Companies House lists Santander UK Group Holdings Plc as the person with significant control of Santander UK plc, notified 6 April 2016, owning 75 percent or more of shares and voting rights; Santander UK plc is a public limited company owned through its own UK holding company, itself part of the Spanish-listed Banco Santander group.

fees.note: Santander's own page for the Everyday Current Account states: "There is no monthly account fee," with "no minimum funding or monthly account fee to keep the account up and running."

accessibility.note: Santander's own Everyday Current Account page states 'No monthly fee' and 'no minimum funding or monthly account fee to keep the account up and running', with switching in seven days through the Current Account Switch Service and fee-free use of Santander cash machines.

products.name: HSBC
products.description: A major global bank that financed billions in fossil fuels in 2025, not a values-aligned choice on climate.

environment.note: The Banking on Climate Chaos 2026 league table ranks HSBC 22nd of the 65 banks it tracks, with $15.9 billion in fossil-fuel financing in 2025.

ethics.note: Companies House states the PSC information for HSBC Holdings plc is not available because, from 30 April 2018, the company has been exempt from the requirement to obtain PSC information as it has voting shares admitted to trading on a UK regulated market; it is registered as a public limited company.

fees.note: HSBC UK's own comparison tool lists "No" against Monthly account fee for the Advance account, and states its current accounts are free to open and come with no monthly fees.

accessibility.note: HSBC's own page for the Advance account says an applicant must 'qualify for an (optional) arranged overdraft of at least £1,000' and be 'happy for us to do a credit check against your name', so this account is gated on credit standing in a way most of the roster is not. HSBC's basic account is not this product.

products.name: Barclays
products.description: One of the largest fossil-fuel financiers on the 2026 Banking on Climate Chaos league table, a clear avoid for a climate-minded customer.

environment.note: The Banking on Climate Chaos 2026 league table ranks Barclays 8th of the 65 banks it tracks, with $34.1 billion in fossil-fuel financing in 2025.

ethics.note: Companies House states the PSC information for Barclays PLC is not available because, from 1 April 2018, the company has been exempt from the requirement to obtain PSC information as it has voting shares admitted to trading on a UK regulated market; it is registered as a public limited company.

fees.note: Barclays' own page for the Barclays Basic Current Account states: "A free account. You won't need to pay any monthly fees," though this basic account carries no overdraft facility.

accessibility.note: Barclays' own page for the Basic Current Account says money can be managed through the Barclays app and 'online, in a branch and by phone', that there are no monthly fees, and that there is no overdraft, arranged or unarranged, which is what makes it available to people other accounts turn down.

products.name: Wells Fargo
products.description: A top-ten fossil financier on the 2026 Banking on Climate Chaos league table.

environment.note: The Banking on Climate Chaos 2026 league table ranks Wells Fargo 6th of the 65 banks it tracks, with $42.5 billion in fossil-fuel financing in 2025.

ethics.note: Wells Fargo & Company's most recent Form 10-K, filed with the SEC, confirms it is a publicly traded company (NYSE: WFC) that answers to public shareholders. A December 20, 2022 CFPB consent order separately found Wells Fargo improperly denied thousands of mortgage loan modifications and ordered close to $3.7 billion in penalties and redress across its auto, mortgage and deposit businesses; that order was terminated in January 2025 after Wells Fargo completed its required actions.

transparency.note: Wells Fargo & Company files an annual Form 10-K with the SEC, the disclosure required of every US public reporting company.

fees.note: Wells Fargo's own page states Everyday Checking carries a $15 (or $0) monthly service fee, waivable by meeting any one of several conditions, including $500 or more in qualifying electronic deposits or a $1,500 minimum daily balance.
